title: Sobha Limited — Risk & Reputation Research
content:
According to reviews, Sobha Limited's customer service is often criticized for being unresponsive, with complaints about slow response to maintenance requests and higher-than-expected service charges. On Trustpilot, one reviewer described Sobha's management staff as "one of the worst" they have encountered, citing unprofessional behavior and poor treatment of apartment owners. On PissedConsumer, the issue resolution rate is reported as low at 0%, and the contact method distribution shows 66% of contacts are made by phone and 34% by email. Despite these complaints, 85% of customers still recommend Sobha to others.

Post-possession service quality varies across Sobha communities. While 85% of customers still recommend Sobha to others, maintenance and after-sales service receives mixed reviews. Common complaints include slow response to maintenance requests, higher-than-expected service charges, and occasional gaps in community management. [...] Common complaints include higher maintenance charges (₹3-4 per sq ft versus industry average of ₹2-3 per sq ft), limited parking spaces in some projects, and occasional delays in amenity completion. Pricing rigidity and perceived lack of negotiation flexibility also feature prominently in customer feedback. [...] Common complaints include higher maintenance charges (₹3-4/sq ft vs industry ₹2-3/sq ft), limited parking spaces in some projects, and occasional delays in amenity completion. However, 85% customers still recommend Sobha to others.

Sobha customers report 78% satisfaction with delivery timelines, significantly above the industry average of 60%. When delays occur, they typically range from 3-6 months and are usually attributed to regulatory approvals or weather-related construction challenges rather than funding issues. Despite improved delivery performance, delays remain a concern for some customers, with average delays of 3-6 months occurring in approximately 22% of projects. Complaints of 6–18 month delays do exist in older projects pre-2017, but Sobha's track record post-2017 is materially cleaner than pre-RERA. Recurring complaints include frustrating customer relationship management during the construction phase and higher maintenance charges due to the amenity stack.

[...] 78% of Sobha customers report on-time possession, with average delays of 3-6 months when they occur. Recent projects show improved delivery with 90% completion within promised timelines, better than industry average of 60%.

### What are common complaints about Sobha projects? [...] Despite improved delivery performance, delays remain a concern for some customers. Average delays of 3-6 months occur in approximately 22% of projects, typically due to regulatory approvals or weather-related construction challenges. Issues in Karnataka real estate appear project-specific and generally resolved through regulatory or CRM channels.

That said, complaints of 6–18 month delays do exist in older projects (pre-2017, pre-RERA era), and some buyers at Dream Acres and Sobha City Gurgaon have flagged later-phase possession slippages. Post-RERA, legal recourse is clearer — possession dates are now legally enforceable — but buyers at large township projects (50+ acres, 5,000+ units) should budget for the possibility of minor phase-level delays. Sobha's track record post-2017 is materially cleaner than pre-RERA. [...] Recurring complaints buyers raise: Customer relationship management during the construction phase can be frustrating — slow responses, interest levied immediately on delayed payments while buyers wait months for resolution of developer-side issues. Modular kitchens, wardrobes, and ACs are typically not included in the base price, despite being manufactured in-house, which catches first-time buyers off guard. Maintenance charges run higher than non-branded societies due to the amenity stack. [...] largely delivered as promised. Resale liquidity is strong — Sobha homes in Bangalore's tech corridors see consistent demand, and rental yields of 3–4% are cited by owners in established communities like Dream Acres. Maintenance through Sobha Facilities Services covers 21,000+ units across 118 projects, with a 48-hour service SLA.

Administrative delays can amplify this effect. In one quarter, Sobha could not recognise over ₹650 crore of revenue simply because occupation certificates were delayed — despite projects being ready.  
To counter this lag, management focuses on embedded metrics: >unrecognised revenue backlog  
>embedded project-level margins  
>margin trajectory of projects nearing completion  
This is why reported margins may look weak even when the business is actually strengthening underneath. [...] This is why Sobha rarely faces large-scale delivery credibility issues compared to many peers.
3.   Sales, Pre-Sales, and Demand: Where the Real Signals AreBecause Sobha recognises revenue only at completion, reported revenue is a lagging indicator.  
What matters instead is what has already been sold.

The sources indicate that Sobha Limited is involved in a legal dispute related to profiteering under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, as per a final order dated 02/04/2026 by the GST Appellate Tribunal. Additionally, there is a consumer protection case against Sobha Limited regarding the payment of Pre-EMI interest, which was contested in a commission on 13 May 2024. There is also a Facebook post seeking a lawyer to file a case against Sobha Limited, but no specific details are provided in the sources.

Sobha Limited has faced criticism regarding its customer service and transparency. Reviews on Trustpilot highlight hidden issues, poor communication, and a lack of responsibility, advising potential buyers to proceed with caution. An in-depth review by APNA VAASTU notes a significant gap between Sobha's polished brand image and low user-review aggregates on platforms like MouthShut, with recurring after-sales complaints and premium pricing. The company also struggles with administrative delays and revenue recognition issues, which can distort financial reports.

Sobha’s reputation for “luxury” does not match the reality we experienced. Instead of professionalism, we encountered hidden issues, poor communication, and a total absence of responsibility.  
⚠️ I strongly advise anyone considering Sobha to proceed with extreme caution. [...] Even worse than the financial discrepancies has been the lack of transparency and accountability. Emails go unanswered, promises are ignored, and customer service feels careless and unprofessional. For a company that presents itself as a premium, international developer, this level of support is shocking. [...] This isn’t just poor customer service — it’s deceptive. They profited from my purchase and then refused to apply the discount that influenced my decision to buy in the first place.  
If you are considering buying from Sobha Realty, be warned: they are not transparent, they do not act in good faith, and once they have your money, they will hide behind excuses rather than honour their commitments.  
I strongly advise anyone thinking about investing with Sobha Realty to reconsider.

Bangalore-specific MouthShut aggregate ratings for Sobha sit surprisingly low (roughly 1.6/5 in aggregate on some project listings), while the Gurgaon-specific listing sits around 1.9/5 — a sharp contrast to the polished 4-to-4.5-star brand image found elsewhere. This gap between “brand reputation” and “raw user-review aggregate” is worth noting explicitly, since most articles cite only the favourable side. This creates several distortions:  
> sales and marketing costs are booked immediately  
> interest costs accumulate during construction  
> high-margin revenue gets deferred  
As a result, current P&L numbers often reflect: projects sold during earlier years, periods of higher input inflation (2021–2023), legacy pricing, not current market rates
